dct_description_sm: This project is part of a larger IPY study, CiCAT, that is looking at the effect of climate change on arctic tundra ecosystems. For our project, we will be collecting Mtis traditional knowledge on vegetation and terrain changes in the North Slave region. In addition, we will be collecting scientific samples to contribute to research partners, and providing traditional knowledge (TK) commentary on the scientific methodology for the larger CiCAT project. We hope to provide an integral component to this IPY project, connecting and melding scientific studies with knowledge from people that live on the land.  One of the goals for IPY is to better understand how northern environments are changing due to climate change. However, science alone cannot answer these questions. Mtis people have lived on the land for many generations and have first hand knowledge, as well as recorded historical knowledge and observations on how the land has been changing. Bringing together these sources of knowledge, we hope to better understand the changes that have occurred and prepare ourselves for changes that are soon to come.
